0.12.1: the pipeline check no longer counts files that were already changed before the task started; the start names them and asks once what to do with them.
0.12.0: new /framegate:pipeline does the deploy / CI changes a task leaves (same pull request, or pipeline/<name>); setup is one table to confirm, filled by `framegate probe`; Dockerfile, compose and CI files are locked by name.
0.11.2: the final brief lists the spec's steps one by one with how each went, then struggles and decisions; brief lines name the file to open; both briefs are shown the same way.
0.11.1: with a state branch the local work branch is always renamed (also with branch = false), the migration cleans framegate's lines out of .gitignore, and doctor no longer warns when the project has no template copy.
0.11.0: shared repositories: framegate's files can live on a separate framegate/<base> branch and `framegate publish` pushes a product-only branch for the pull request; ports get stubs from the reference, kept quirks and a reference follow-up.
0.10.0: every feature, bug fix and refactor now starts with a check that brings the command-line tool and the project's tools to this version; agents use the project's own Python and commands; the PR phase is now called SUMMARY.
0.9.0: setup files (pyproject.toml, pytest.ini, framegate.toml) are edited in the spec phase and committed with "spec OK"; specs can name read-only reference projects and what is ported from them; deploy / CI changes become a pipeline follow-up.
0.8.0: framegate now keeps itself up to date: the command-line tool follows the plugin's version when you start a feature, and you see one line like this after an update.
0.7.0: step checks now run the whole normal test suite, the final checks fail on assertions that never ran, and answers that only take the defaults no longer repeat every check.
